title: Check: Trends in the Periodic Table

questions.stem: What happens to atomic radius going across a period from left to right?
questions.explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period because the number of protons increases while electrons are added to the same shell. The greater nuclear charge pulls the outer electrons closer to the nucleus, making the atoms smaller.

questions.stem: Why does ionisation energy decrease going down a group?

options.text: The outer electrons are further from the nucleus with more shielding, so less energy is needed to remove them

questions.explanation: Going down a group, atoms have more electron shells, so outer electrons are further from the nucleus. There is also more shielding from inner electrons. Both effects weaken the attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron, meaning less energy is needed to remove it.
